claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you, and I'd be happy to help assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask a few more questions:

**Is Alex living with you?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you!

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and upbringing, such as paying for his food, clothing, and other necessities?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually a bit complicated. Alex has been in care with the local authority for a few months now. He's living in a children's home at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important detail. I understand these situations can be complex.

Let me just read the relevant guidance to make sure I give you accurate information about Child Benefit when a child is in local authority care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I have a few follow-up questions about Alex's situation in care:

**How long has Alex been in the local authority children's home?** (Specifically, has it been more than 8 weeks?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been about 3 months now, so that's more than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Since Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks, there's an important question that will determine your eligibility:

**Does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you?** (For example, does he come home for regular visits that add up to at least 24 hours per week?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home that often. He stays at the children's home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being so open with me about Alex's situation.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me provide you with my determination.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- Alex has been in local authority care for approximately 3 months, which is longer than the 8-week threshold.
- Under the Child Benefit rules, entitlement to Child Benefit usually ends once a child has been in care for more than 8 weeks.
- There is an exception if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you, but since Alex stays at the children's home full-time, this exception doesn't apply.

**Important to know:** If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he starts spending at least 2 nights in a row each week at home, or 7 or more days in a row with you—you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. If that happens, I'd recommend contacting HMRC to discuss your options.

I understand this may not be the news you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help you with?
